papers.title: OA-RAG: Ontology-based Agentic RAG for Faithful LLM Reasoning
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform well across many real-world tasks but remain prone to hallucination, limiting their reliability in domains such as biomedicine and healthcare, where answers must be grounded in established knowledge. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) mitigates this problem by incorporating external information, but often overlooks logical relationships and relies heavily on the LLM's own reasoning, which can compromise answer faithfulness. We propose OA-RAG, an agent that integrates formal reasoning with LLM reasoning, drawing on both the logical structure and informal annotations of domain ontologies. For each answer, OA-RAG reports the ontology observations used as evidence and a model-assessed grounding level (entailed, supported, related, or unrelated) that characterises the strength of that evidence. Across benchmarks derived from three large-scale ontologies and six real-world medical question-answering tasks, OA-RAG achieves the best overall performance among the evaluated ontology-fine-tuned and popular RAG methods, with particularly strong results on reasoning-intensive tasks. The reported grounding levels also offer a useful indication of answer reliability, with stronger grounding generally associated with higher accuracy. Finally, our results demonstrate the value of ontologies as knowledge sources: OA-RAG is competitive with, and sometimes outperforms, domain-specific RAG systems that draw on sources such as textbooks.
papers.llm_summary: OA-RAG: agentic RAG kết hợp reasoning ontology hình thức với LLM, báo grounding level (entailed/supported/related/unrelated) cho mỗi câu trả lời, benchmark 6 task QA y tế.
papers.llm_reason: Agentic RAG/chống hallucination core rất cao (31), benchmark 3 ontology + 6 task thật, SOTA (23), grounding level directly applicable cho content fact-checking/decision (15+13), insight hành động rõ nhất nhóm.

papers.title: Ask Before You Answer: A Question-Driven Evidence Reasoning Architecture (QERA) for In-Context Learning
papers.abstract: AI assistants are increasingly asked to reason over a user's own web traces: group chats, community threads, activity logs and revision histories. On CL-bench Life, a benchmark of such real-life context learning, frontier LLMs solve fewer than one task in five. We find that the request is not the specification: over 80% of the benchmark's rubrics share less than 60% of their content words with the final request, as for a rule set two turns earlier or every record that meets the user's criterion, and LLMs answering directly pass only 67% of these implicit rubrics against 81% of the others. We propose QERA, a Question-driven Evidence Reasoning Architecture that asks before it answers. QERA first turns the request into a requirement checklist and typed information needs, filtered by code for faithfulness to the user's words; it then answers from the whole conversation, asks the same questions again with quotes verified by code, and applies a guarded local repair. It needs no training or rubrics and makes about four LLM calls per task. On all 405 tasks with four frontier LLMs, QERA attains the highest solving rate on every LLM (21.0% on average, against 18.2% for the strongest of three inference-time baselines and 14.6% for direct answering) and leads every baseline significantly when pooled across LLMs, while using fewer tokens than PSCI and 4-5% of the tokens of Ctx2Skill. Ablations on GPT-6-Luna show that the gain is settled before the answer, by a fixed answer protocol (+3.8 rubric points) and the request-specific questions (+1.6), and that it is concentrated on implicit rubrics, with checking afterwards refining mainly numeric requirements.
papers.llm_summary: QERA biến request thành checklist yêu cầu, đặt câu hỏi làm rõ trước khi trả lời, đạt solving rate cao nhất trên 405 tác vụ với 4 LLM frontier mà không cần huấn luyện thêm.
papers.llm_reason: Insight 'hỏi trước khi trả lời' cực kỳ actionable cho prompt engineering, content creation và tương tác khách hàng; thí nghiệm mạnh, áp dụng ngay được vào workflow LLM hàng ngày.

papers.title: From Faulty Claims to Incorrect Patches: An Empirical Study of Task-Grounded Reasoning in Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based coding agents increasingly resolve real-world software engineering tasks, yet still fail on many of them. Prior trajectory studies characterize these failures through task-agnostic patterns of agent behavior, such as repeated actions. However, an agent may follow a sound workflow yet act on a faulty understanding of the existing code, the task requirements, or a candidate fix. Reasoning models, which power most state-of-the-art coding agents, reveal this understanding in their native chain-of-thought (CoT), whose claims about the task can be checked against the facts. Yet it remains unclear how many such checkable claims the CoT contains, how many are faulty, and whether faulty claims actually cause incorrect patches. We present the first empirical study of such claims, which we term task-grounded reasoning, analyzing 400 trajectories of four open-weight reasoning models on SWE-bench Pro. We extract atomic claims from the CoT with an LLM, assess them against evidence gathered by an LLM agent, and manually trace the defects of incorrect patches back to faulty claims, confirming each link with a claim-corrected replay. Task-grounded reasoning covers only 18.5% of the CoT tokens, yet yields 191 atomic claims per trajectory, at least 9.6% of which are faulty. Faulty claims also occur in 96.7% of the resolved trajectories, so their mere presence is a weak signal of failure. Yet two thirds of the 188 incorrect patches trace back to faulty claims. Correcting such a claim makes the agent fix the linked defect in 89.0% of the cases, and correcting all such claims resolves 11.7% of the failed tasks. Our findings show that the CoT carries task-specific signals for diagnosing and repairing agent failures, but exploiting them requires pinpointing the few faulty claims that actually cause patch defects.
papers.llm_summary: Nghiên cứu 400 trajectory SWE-bench Pro: CoT coding agent chứa 191 claims/trajectory, ≥9.6% faulty, và faulty claims là nguyên nhân patch sai ngay cả ở task đã resolve.
papers.llm_reason: Coding agent + CoT verification sát cách dùng AI hàng ngày (31), empirical lớn + replay xác nhận nhân quả (21), giúp solopreneur đánh giá agent viết code (12), actionable: audit claims trước khi tin patch (15).

papers.title: Topology-Conditioned Backdoors: Language Models That Insert Vulnerabilities When They Infer They Are in a Multi-Agent System
papers.abstract: A language model may behave safely in a single-agent evaluation yet produce vulnerable code when its context suggests that it is part of a multi-agent system. We study this failure mode by fine-tuning Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to condition code generation on deployment topology inferred from prompt-level provenance cues. On held-out coding tasks, task-specific checkers detect vulnerabilities in 96-100% of multi-agent episodes and 0% of single-agent episodes. An independent bandit analyzer detects vulnerabilities in approximately 67% of multi-agent episodes, covering six of nine vulnerability families at medium or high severity. Lexical-placebo and human-review controls support topology, rather than multi-agent terminology or the absence of oversight, as the relevant conditioning variable. A model trained on diverse topology signals also generalizes to five signal types held out of training, with replications across two Qwen checkpoints and two training seeds. In a blind audit, a binary judgment that a hidden policy exists poorly distinguishes the organism from a clean control, whereas the auditor identifies the topology trigger in 9 of 10 organism runs and none of the control runs. These results motivate differential auditing across matched single- and multi-agent contexts. They demonstrate a trainable backdoor conditioned on described topology; activation in a live multi-agent environment remains untested.
papers.llm_summary: Cài backdoor vào LLM khiến nó sinh code có lỗ hổng chỉ khi nhận ra đang trong multi-agent system, kích hoạt 96-100% multi-agent và 0% single-agent.
papers.llm_reason: Cảnh báo bảo mật multi-agent thiết yếu cho ai dùng agent, experiment nghiêm ngặt nhiều control, nhưng ứng dụng business trực tiếp ở mức trung bình.

papers.title: EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis
papers.abstract: Deploying LLM agents in specialized domains often require fine-grained task-specific procedures and knowledge a general model lacks, yet parameter training is costly and non-interpretable, and hand-engineered agent systems shift the cost to expert labor. Episodic memory updates at context level, but single agent adaptation struggles to alleviate cross-task interference, especially with complex tasks such as multi-application navigation or data pool analysis. Although multi-agent evolution alleviates this problem, existing methods lack clear definitions on update rules and rely on the backbone model to decide where and how much the system changes. This ill-scoped evolution makes learning follow the backbone's structural preferences rather than the observed failures: one backbone accumulates skills while another spawns agents. We present EMMA (structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent workflow synthesis), which treats the configuration of a multi-agent system (controller routing memory, specialists inheriting a generalist prompt, and per-step procedural skills) as episodic memory. EMMA makes the ownership and admissibility of updates explicit: a reflector assigns each diagnosed failure to the scope owning its correction and proposes one edit within it, and backbone-independent guards keep every accepted edit scoped, incremental and bounded. Across KramaBench, AppWorld and BBEH with five backbones and four baselines (ACE, GEPA, EvoMAS and ADAS), EMMA attains the best overall performance on every benchmark, up to 32.5% over the strongest baseline, maintains consistent improvements across backbones, and uses 17-38% fewer training executions than the most efficient baseline.
papers.llm_summary: EMMA tổng hợp workflow đa agent bằng episodic memory có cấu trúc, tự chẩn đoán lỗi và cập nhật từng bước mà không cần fine-tune.
papers.llm_reason: Rất liên quan: workflow synthesis áp dụng trực tiếp vào pipeline content đa kênh, episodic memory giúp học từ mỗi bài viết, insight hành động rõ ràng.

papers.title: Governed Sovereign RAG for Public Administration: Tripartite Epistemic Routing, Facet-Guided Clarification, and Deterministic Numeric Verification in Citizen Services
papers.abstract: Deploying conversational assistants at government service desks faces a tension between regulatory certainty (zero tolerance for invented fees), data sovereignty prohibiting commercial clouds, and high rates of underspecified or out-of-jurisdiction citizen queries. We present and evaluate a governed, sovereign Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture deployed on the official portal of the State of Tlaxcala, Mexico (tlaxcaladigital.gob.mx), covering 1,143 procedures and a decoupled directory of 924 offices. The system governs interactions via three pillars: (1) a two-stage tripartite epistemic gate (clarify_policy and a Boltzmann distribution over AnyJev) arbitrating among answering (SPECIFIC), facet-guided clarification (CLARIFY), and abstaining (ABSTAIN); (2) a post-generation deterministic numeric verifier (verify_numeric_guardrail) with SHA-256 cache invalidation ensuring every generated fee or validity figure belongs to the retrieved official record; and (3) an empirical evaluation across 380 organic production traces (8 weeks) and a 200-query stratified benchmark (5-fold CV: 86.41% +/- 7.50%). In production, 89.47% of traffic is resolved at Level 0 via deterministic templates without free generation (global p50 = 0.665 s; direct L0 p50 = 0.445 s; slow-tail p95 = 30.412 s under CPU queuing), with 0/40 fiscal amount hallucinations observed in Level 1 (95% bound <= 8.81%). On the benchmark, the system achieves 86.50% strict Top-1 accuracy (+10.00 pp over a binary neural gate, p = 0.00453, p_Holm = 0.01172), pairing a 93.00% conditional safe upper bound with a 70.87% dropout-adjusted effective resolution after accounting for 53.33% citizen drop-off in clarification menus.
papers.llm_summary: RAG sovereign cho cổng chính phủ Mexico với gate trả lời/làm rõ/từ chối + verifier số deterministic, triển khai thật 1.143 thủ tục, 0 hallucination phí trong 400 case.
papers.llm_reason: RAG/routing/abstain rất core (28), production thật + benchmark 5-fold CV (23), governance nội dung & chống sai lệch phù hợp content business (12), pattern CLARIFY/ABSTAIN + verify có thể copy (15).

papers.title: MAS-Gate: Unlocking Multi-Agent System Lifecycle via Node-Centric Quantification
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) can solve complex problems beyond the reach of a single agent by decomposing tasks and coordinating complementary capabilities. Despite extensive research on MAS, existing work largely focuses on specific aspects or individual phases of their development and operation, resulting in fragmented perspectives with objectives and signals that are difficult to reconcile across these different settings. To bridge these disconnected perspectives, we conceptualize MAS development and operation as a three-phase lifecycle spanning design-time orchestration before execution, runtime intervention during execution, and post-hoc attribution after execution, and introduce MAS-Gate, a unified node-centric quantification applicable across these phases. Modeling each execution as a directed acyclic graph, MAS-Gate combines within-node utility, which estimates a node's contribution through changes in reference-answer likelihood, with inter-node strength, which approximates semantic uptake and potential downstream reach. We adapt this shared quantification to three objectives: providing a structure-aware dense reward for Orchestrator training, training an Editor to act on execution prefixes using paired rewards from completed edited and unedited trajectories, and supplying risk-ranked nodes as auxiliary evidence for LLM-based post-hoc attribution. Experiments spanning interaction environments, knowledge-intensive multi-hop question answering, general reasoning, and post-hoc attribution demonstrate that MAS-Gate improves workflow construction, targeted runtime editing, and LLM-assisted error localization over corresponding phase-specific baselines. Together, these results establish MAS-Gate as a unified structural interface for improving MAS generation, dynamic editing, and error attribution throughout the lifecycle.
papers.llm_summary: MAS-Gate mô hình hóa vòng đời multi-agent (thiết kế–runtime–post-hoc) thành DAG với lượng hóa node-centric để huấn luyện Orchestrator, Editor và attribution.
papers.llm_reason: Core multi-agent/orchestration cao, có ứng dụng thật qua rewards/dense evidence, giúp solopreneur hiểu và thiết kế workflow agent cho nội dung.

papers.title: FlowMAS: Learning Multi-Agent Workflow Topology via Information-guided Generative Flow Network
papers.abstract: Automated multi-agent systems offer clear advantages over manually designed ones in scalability and adaptability, but existing workflow topology methods still face important limitations. Search-based methods are often computationally expensive, textual-gradient-based methods rely on coarse-grained feedback, and existing generation-based methods are not well suited to discrete workflow topologies with complex dependencies. To address these limitations, we propose FlowMAS, a multi-agent workflow topology method based on Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets). FlowMAS models workflow generation as reward-guided flow over the topology space and introduces three components: a GFlowNet-based topology generation backbone, a curiosity-driven module for structure-aware exploration, and an information-guided optimization module for evaluating intermediate topologies. Concretely, the curiosity-driven module encourages exploration of structurally novel workflows, while the information-guided module measures both the information contribution and the communication efficiency of different operators to favor more informative and effective collaboration patterns. Experiments on six benchmark datasets with three LLM backbones show that FlowMAS consistently outperforms multiple baselines.
papers.llm_summary: FlowMAS tự động sinh topology workflow multi-agent bằng GFlowNets với module好奇 explores cấu trúc mới và tối ưu theo thông tin/hiệu quả giao tiếp.
papers.llm_reason: Multi-agent workflow rất liên quan, benchmark 6 dataset/3 backbone vững, hữu ích để tự động hóa chuỗi agent làm content nhưng khá kỹ thuật.

papers.title: ClinAgent: A ReAct-Based Agent for Conversational Access to Clinical Trial Information
papers.abstract: Querying clinical trial registries remains a manual and error-prone process, requiring researchers to navigate large volumes of semi-structured data without support for natural language interaction or cross-source synthesis. To address this, we introduce ClinAgent, a conversational system based on agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) that enables clinicians and researchers to query clinical trial information in plain language and receive grounded, up-to-date responses across multi-turn interactions. The system centers on a Large Language Model (LLM) agent following the ReAct paradigm, which iteratively reasons over queries, selects among a set of integrated tools, and refines its actions based on intermediate outputs. These tools include a ClinicalTrials.gov search interface, a PubMed module, and a Python-based analyzer operating on a locally cached structured dataset of clinical trials. We evaluate the system using a three-phase framework assessing operational effectiveness, planning quality, tool-use efficiency, and expert qualitative judgments, comparing three LLM backends: Gemini 3.0 Flash and two variants of DeepSeek V3.2 (thinking and non-thinking). Results reveal complementary strengths, with DeepSeek (thinking mode) excelling in planning quality, while Gemini achieves the highest overall performance and strongest expert ratings. Overall, our findings highlight the potential of agentic AI systems to improve the accessibility and synthesis of clinical trial information, supporting more efficient and user-centered biomedical research workflows.
papers.llm_summary: Xây dựng ClinAgent, agent ReAct RAG tích hợp tools (ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed, Python analyzer) để truy vấn thông tin thử nghiệm lâm sàng bằng ngôn ngữ tự nhiên, so sánh hiệu năng 3 backend LLM.
papers.llm_reason: ReAct agent + tool-use chính là kiến trúc solopreneur có thể copy để xây research assistant cho nội dung AI, evaluation 3 giai đoạn so sánh Gemini vs DeepSeek rất thực tiễn và đọc xong biết chọn model.

papers.title: DRILS: Dependency-based Requirement Change Impact Analysis Using LLMs
papers.abstract: Change is inevitable in software systems, where requirements must continuously adapt to evolving stakeholder needs, regulations, and project scopes. Managing such changes is a fundamental software engineering challenge, as manually identifying the impact of a change request, given high requirements volume, Natural Language (NL) complexity, and intricate interdependencies, is error-prone and time-consuming. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer promising solutions for requirements change impact analysis (CIA), yet their effectiveness when enhanced with advanced techniques remains underexplored. We present DRILS, an LLM-based agentic framework for requirements Change Impact Analysis, employing a multi-agent architecture to generate candidate impact sets, with an LLM-as-a-judge promoting diversity during selection. DRILS features two key components: RE-RAG, a carefully engineered RAG technique providing focused domain context, and a requirement dependency graph (RDG) as an additional knowledge source. Evaluation across three manually curated datasets demonstrates superior performance over state-of-the-art baselines, achieving an average recall of 87.1%, precision of 76.3%, and F1 score of 81% at a lower cost. Precision gains are particularly significant, 41.1%, 83.4%, and 149.8% over the closest baseline per dataset, as higher precision directly reduces false positives and manual validation effort. We also contribute three annotated CIA datasets to support future research.
papers.llm_summary: Xây dựng DRILS, framework multi-agent LLM với RE-RAG và requirement dependency graph cộng LLM-as-judge để phân tích tác động thay đổi yêu cầu phần mềm, đạt F1 81%, precision cao hơn baseline tới 149.8%.
papers.llm_reason: Pattern multi-agent + RAG + dependency graph + LLM-as-judge với metric thật, chi phí thấp, dễ mượn cho planning/đánh giá tác động roadmap content, nhưng domain requirements engineering làm giảm liên quan trực tiếp.
